lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: choosing a helper job

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Ready for Life elementary sequence — Grade 3
Ready for Life v1 safety, supervision, and no-shame policy reference
Manuel Academy RFL G3 Unit 6 — family contribution capstone
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice choosing a helper job. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: Before any cleaning or sorting happens, the learner sits down with a written list of six ordinary jobs that exist in almost any home and a blank sheet of paper.
materials: adult-or-local: a written or printed list of six household helper job options

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u06-l01-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u06-l01-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u06-l01-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u06-l01-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Explain the specific reason you picked this job over the other five options, based on something you noticed while comparing them, not just 'it seemed easiest.'

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u06-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g3-u06-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g3-u06-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Comparison across options: Compares at least three job options using both questions (steps, adult nearby) before picking one. | Job specificity: The picked job is named with a specific location and a general sense of what it involves. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u06-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner list two more household jobs not on the original six-job list that would also count as a family helper job, using the same two questions (steps and adult-nearby) to check that each one qualifies.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can practice choosing a helper job. I will do one step at a time and check one result.

duration.sessionPattern: 5 minutes model, 5–7 minutes guided try, 10–15 minutes learner task, 5 minutes evidence and retry check
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: a written or printed list of six household helper job options
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

localMaterials.label: paper and a pencil
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: choosing a helper job worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Before any cleaning or sorting happens, the learner sits down with a written list of six ordinary jobs that exist in almost any home and a blank sheet of paper.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact choosing a helper job decision or action.
Model move 2: Before picking anything, read through the full list of six job options once without deciding yet.
Model move 3: For each of the six jobs, ask the two questions — about how many steps this takes and whether an adult would need to be nearby — and mark a quick answer before moving to the next job.

Model check: Comparison across options: Compares at least three job options using both questions (steps, adult nearby) before picking one. | Job specificity: The picked job is named with a specific location and a general sense of what it involves.

resources.title: choosing a helper job action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for choosing a helper job.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u06-l01-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g3-u06-l01-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g3-u06-l01-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g3-u06-l01-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g3-u06-l01-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: choosing a helper job coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Before any cleaning or sorting happens, the learner sits down with a written list of six ordinary jobs that exist in almost any home and a blank sheet of paper.
Coach direction: Before picking anything, read through the full list of six job options once without deciding yet.
Learner prompt: Name one job from the list that you have never fully done before.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: choosing a helper job complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: For each of the six jobs, ask the two questions — about how many steps this takes and whether an adult would need to be nearby — and mark a quick answer before moving to the next job.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I read all six job options before ranking or picking any of them.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I estimated the number of steps for at least three different jobs, not just my favorite one.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I noted for each job whether an adult would need to be nearby for any part of it.
Response 4 (t2-p4): I picked exactly one job, not two, as my choice for this unit.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: choosing a helper job minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain the specific reason you picked this job over the other five options, based on something you noticed while comparing them, not just 'it seemed easiest.'

Success checks: Comparison across options: Compares at least three job options using both questions (steps, adult nearby) before picking one. | Job specificity: The picked job is named with a specific location and a general sense of what it involves.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: choosing a helper job supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g3-u06-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g3-u06-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional choosing a helper job condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Comparison across options: Compares at least three job options using both questions (steps, adult nearby) before picking one. | Job specificity: The picked job is named with a specific location and a general sense of what it involves..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u06-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: Before any cleaning or sorting happens, the learner sits down with a written list of six ordinary jobs that exist in almost any home and a blank sheet of paper.
guidedFirstAttempt.prompt: Name one job from the list that you have never fully done before.
coachMoves: Ask the learner to name the condition.
Point to one model step only.
Give feedback against one observable success check.
guidedFirstAttempt.successCondition: Comparison across options: Compares at least three job options using both questions (steps, adult nearby) before picking one.
guidedFirstAttempt.correctionTurn: Use the fresh condition on swk-rfl-g3-u06-l01-guided-card: change one constraint, redo only the affected move, and state why the corrected move now meets the success check.

simulationRoute.title: choosing a helper job — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the choosing a helper job task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Explain the specific reason you picked this job over the other five options, based on something you noticed while comparing them, not just 'it seemed easiest.'
observableCriteria: Comparison across options: Compares at least three job options using both questions (steps, adult nearby) before picking one.
Job specificity: The picked job is named with a specific location and a general sense of what it involves.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u06-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g3-u06-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g3-u06-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Comparison across options: Compares at least three job options using both questions (steps, adult nearby) before picking one. | Job specificity: The picked job is named with a specific location and a general sense of what it involves.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u06-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
